news.headline: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift
news.story_lead: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift Maharashtra's Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone, the IMD study showed. India’s climate is turning hotter and drier, with large parts of north India changing from temperate to arid steppe and from hot and tropical Savannah to temperate, hot-summer, between 1961 and 2020, a 70-year analysis of rainfall and temperature changes conducted by researchers at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has found. The study also found that India’s peninsular region (excluding the Central Deccan Plateau centred around Maharashtra’s Vidarbha and Marathwada regions), on the other hand, has shifted towards the wetter zone, from arid steppe hot to tropical savannah.
news.full_article_text: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift Maharashtra's Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone, the IMD study showed. India’s climate is turning hotter and drier, with large parts of north India changing from temperate to arid steppe and from hot and tropical Savannah to temperate, hot-summer, between 1961 and 2020, a 70-year analysis of rainfall and temperature changes conducted by researchers at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has found. The study also found that India’s peninsular region (excluding the Central Deccan Plateau centred around Maharashtra’s Vidarbha and Marathwada regions), on the other hand, has shifted towards the wetter zone, from arid steppe hot to tropical savannah. Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone. What the study points out The study titled: Identifying the climate zone shifts of Indian meteorological subdivisions: insights from historical records, by Ananya Karmakar, Rajib Chattopadhyay, Pulak Guhathakurta, K S Hosalikar and Mrutyunjay Mohapatra of the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, is published in MAUSAM, IMD's peer-reviewed journal, this month. The study had set out to investigate historical records of shifts in climate zone modulation across Indian meteorological subdivisions, aiming to uncover the underlying drivers and patterns that have shaped India's climate landscape by examining historical data, including meteorological observations, proxy records, and historical accounts. “Two significant findings came out of this analysis -- over the historical period 1951–2020, the major change in the climate zone is the shift to the drier region, i.e. temperate to arid steppe and hot and tropical Savannah to temperate hot summer for the North West and North East homogeneous regions, respectively. The percentage area transformed to the drier region is nearly 7% in both homogeneous regions. This modulation is mainly associated with the increasing trend in temperature and decreasing trend in rainfall,” the study has noted. “For the Peninsular India homogeneous region, the climate zones shift towards the wetter zone, from Arid steppe hot to Tropical savannah by 15% due to a mainly increasing trend of rainfall in recent epochs,” the study also noted. “But interior Maharashtra, including Marathwada and west Vidarbha, which lay mostly in the tropical savannah zone, which is warm throughout the year with a long dry season, but by 1991–2020 they had moved into the hot semi-arid zone, which is hot with low rainfall, a change the authors attribute mainly to rising daytime and night-time temperatures,” lead study author Ananya Karmakar said. Climate zones are defined by temperature and rainfall, and the researchers redrew India's climate map for successive 30-year periods (epochs), the standard span over which climate is measured, from 1951–1980 to 1991–2020, using IMD's own observations. The study noted that between 1961–1990, along the coast, the tropical monsoon zone, the country's wettest, with heavy seasonal rain, has extended further across the Konkan, Goa, coastal Karnataka and Kerala. The spread of the wettest zone along the coast is consistent with a broader pattern in the study, in which rainfall has increased over southern India even as it has declined over the northern plains, resulting in Maharashtra's interior and its coastline changing in opposite directions. “The current shrinking and expected disappearance of the tropical savannah and temperate climate zone will cause numerous problems related to food safety and local population displacement. This is something that must be taken into account in future socioeconomic development plans for the country. Overall, the results suggest that the increasing influence of the negative phase of the Victoria Mode plays a pivotal role in modulating rainfall variability and driving the expansion of drier climate classes over Northern India. The continued contraction of tropical savannah and temperate climate zones poses serious risks to food security, water resources, and regional livelihoods. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating large-scale climate variability into long-term agricultural planning and climate adaptation strategies in India,” Karmakar noted. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Gerard de Souza Gerard de Souza is a Special Correspondent based in Goa and has been reporting on and about issues concerning the state and the wider western coast of India for over 18 years. news.full_article_text: Students win Viksit Bharat Buildathon for bomb-diffusing robot, smart glasses The national winners included students from Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh A spider-shaped bomb-diffusing robot developed by students in Assam, affordable bone-conduction smart glasses designed by a Uttar Pradesh team and an urban air-purification concept from Gujarat were among the 10 national-level winners of the Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025, which entered the Guinness World Records as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition” with 287,967 project submissions across both idea and prototype tracks. The 10 winning teams received a combined cash prize of ₹ 17.50 lakh, while the nationwide initiative had an award pool of more than ₹ 1 crore across district, state and national levels. The national awards comprised five winners in the prototype track, each receiving ₹ 2.5 lakh for their working models, and five in the idea track, each awarded ₹ 1 lakh to encourage further development of their concepts. The idea track recognises students who present innovative concepts to address real-world problems, while the prototype track rewards teams that develop functional working models of their proposed solutions. Union minister of state (MoS) for education Jayant Chaudhary felicitated the winning teams in New Delhi on Wednesday at an event in New Delhi and received the Guinness World Records certification for the initiative which Union education ministry hailed as “a historic milestone for school education and grassroots innovation in India” Organised by the department of school education and literacy under the Union education ministry, in collaboration with NITI Aayog’s Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), the programme launched in September 2025 aims to encourage school students to identify real-world problems and develop solutions independently. Also Read: CM Modi to PM Modi: A tale of continuity and evolution The winning projects addressed challenges spanning public safety, renewable energy, urban pollution, environmental sustainability and livelihoods. A three-tier assessment process at the district, state and national levels, conducted by multidisciplinary expert panels, selected 10 national awardees, 100 state awardees and 1,000 district awardees. The national winners included students from Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh. The Assam team from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya, Tinsukia, won for “Vadiffuse”, a spider-shaped robot designed to diffuse bombs. Students from Modern Public School, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, were recognised for their project on renewable energy, while a team from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya No. 1, Surat, Gujarat, developed the “Urban Breathing Pole”. Students from Green Valley Educational Institute, Srinagar, won for “Guardian Bridge”. A team from De Nobili School, Dhanbad, Jharkhand, was recognised for a project exploring methane gas in the coal-mining region, titled “Dhanbad: The Burning Treasure and the Silent Methane Gas”. Other winners included “EcoSync” from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya, Adoor, Kerala; “WINDMINER”, an omnidirectional windmill, from Carmel Convent Senior Secondary School, Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh; and a tasar cocoon counting and quality-checking machine with segregation from DAV Public School, Unit-VIII, Odisha. An “Instant Thermo Flask” developed by students of Pathippaga Chemmal K Ganapathy Government Higher Secondary School, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, and “EchoLens”, affordable bone-conduction smart glasses developed by students of Step by Step School, Rohillapur, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, were among the top 10. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sanjay Maurya Sanjay Maurya is a Principal Correspondent with Hindustan Times, where he covers education, with a focus on school and higher education, competitive examinations, education policy and governance. Working as part of the National Bureau, he is based in New Delhi and reports on the Ministry of Education and covers various statutory bodies like UGC, AICTE and NCTE and autonomous bodies like CBSE and NCERT. His reporting also tracks the implementation of key government reforms and policies from school education to higher education including in IITs, NITs, IIMs, central and state universities, and their impact on students and educational institutions. His reporting on the irregularities and rushed implementation of CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluation of Class 12 board exams 2026, triggered administrative action, leading to the transfer of the board's two senior-most officials and the constitution of a committee to probe alleged irregularities in procurement process of the system. news.full_article_text: Trans rights safeguards pose practical issues, govt tells Supreme Court The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that considering protective provisions for transgender people’s rights can throw up practical challenges, with trans women accessing benefits and asserting rights otherwise available to biological women under various statutes The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that considering protective provisions for transgender people’s rights can throw up practical challenges, with trans women accessing benefits and asserting rights otherwise available to biological women under various statutes. With the validity of Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 separately being challenged before the top court, solicitor- general Tushar Mehta said that he will address this concern among others in the Centre’s affidavit responding to a batch of petitions challenging the law’s validity on multiple grounds. “My reply is getting ready. I will reply on this aspect too,” Mehta said. The concerns were brought before the court on Wednesday in a fresh petition by the India chapter of a women’s organisation called Women’s Declaration International, which said that while transgenders have a right to their identity, they should not be allowed to encroach into the constitutional and statutory benefits available to biological women. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant agreed to hear the matter and asked senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner along with advocate Binsy Susan, to serve a copy of the petition to the solicitor- general. “The matter is sub-judice before us. We do not wish to add another aspect to it. But your perspective is different. According to you, if somebody is a transgender woman, that person should not have the same status as a biological female,” said the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said. Mehta said that several high courts are now faced with the question of whether a man claiming to have the sexual identity of a woman should be allowed to participate in sporting events as a female contestant. The question also arose in jails, wherein if a man identifies as a female, if he is to be kept in a women’s jail. Even under the penal statutes, arresting a woman after sunset is not permissible. This question will be raised with regard to trans women. Also, Mehta added that trans people may insist on being frisked only by female police personnel. Sibal said that even the Constitution reserves seats for women in Panchayats which cannot be encroached upon by trans women. “The Act makes provisions for transgenders. At the same time, there are constitutional and statutory benefits promised to biological females. The question is whether those rights and protections can be encroached upon by transgender persons,” he said. He added that while the petitioner supported the right of transgenders to be identified as the third sex with equal rights available to any person, the implications of the rights that flowed from such identification needed to be determined.

news.full_article_text: New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York A new organisation, RSS Friends registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) on August 27 as a foreign agent representing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), despite the RSS’ previous assertions that it does not lobby in the US. In its filings with the DoJ, RSS Friends explicitly listed the RSS as its “foreign principal” along with the address of the organisation’s new headquarters in Delhi’s Keshav Kunj. The newly registered group also disclosed that its work will remain primarily informational, but that it does not have a written employment or lobbying contract with the RSS with specified compensation and deliverables. RSS spokesperson Sunil Ambekar didn’t respond to queries seeking comment despite multiple reminders. RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York. The RSS, celebrating its centenary this year, is the ideological fount of the Bharatiya Janata Party. “RSS Friends’ proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community-engagement activities. Consistent with its governing documents and applicable law, it may communicate with members of the public, journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders, civil-society organisations, and, where appropriate, government agencies or officials,” the filing reads. It added: “The absence of a written contract should not be understood as a representation that no relationship, request, understanding, coordination, authorisation, direction, or other relevant factual connection exists. RSS Friends will disclose the actual facts relevant to its activities.” RSS Friends’ website provides more detail about its objectives, which tend to revolve around correcting “misconceptions about the RSS” pushed by “politically motivated actors” that have created “negative repercussions for the Indian diaspora, particularly Hindu Americans.” It is not clear how old the organisation is, but the rssfriends.org websie was first registered in 2017. It is also not clear when the current version of the website was launched. Three individuals linked with RSS Friends are mentioned in the DoJ filings: Rajendra Sonarikar, Pratikkumar Suthar and Jayant Pant. Suthar’s Linkedin profile says he “coordinates global outreach in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)” and has served in his position since March 2024. Suthar is based in New Delhi while it is presently unclear where Sonarikar and Pant reside. RSS Friends did not respond to a request for comment from HT. The new registration follows a prolonged controversy over the RSS’ lobbying in the United States. In November 2025, news outlet Prism reported that elite lobbying firm Squire Patton Boggs was hired to “introduce the RSS to US officials” through State Street Strategies, another lobbying outfit. Subsequent disclosures filed with the US DoJ showed that Squire Patton Boggs had been paid $330,000 for its work on behalf of the RSS in 2025. To be sure, the RSS categorically denied reports that it hired lobbyists in America. Squire Patton Boggs subsequently disclosed its contract was terminated on September 30, 2025. The matter caused a significant political controversy in India in late 2025. “This is hardly the first time that the RSS has betrayed national interest,” Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said in response to the matter at the time. The registration of RSS Friends coincides with a systematic effort by the RSS to enhance its outreach to the United States. Prior to Mohan Bhagwat’s visit in August this year, the organisation’s second-in-command Dattatreya Hosabale undertook a multi-day tour of America in April. This was explained by Hosabale as an effort to interact with “influential opinion makers” in Western nations to communicate the RSS’ mission and objectives. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shashank Mattoo Shashank Mattoo is the Washington DC-based US Correspondent for Hindustan Times. news.full_article_text: Supreme Court directs Centre to grant war injury pension to Army veteran who developed illness during Kargil posting The bench said the government must go by what its policy actually says and not what it intended it to mean. The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Union government to grant a ‘war injury pension’ to an Indian Army veteran who had developed “rheumatoid arthritis” during his posting at Kargil, ruling that the government cannot interpret its own policy in a way that “contradicts its plain wording” or leads to “arbitrary, irrational or discriminatory outcomes.” A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed an appeal filed by the Union government challenging previous orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and the High Court that had directed it to pay the veteran, Narendra Kumar, a war injury pension instead of disability pension. “While interpreting the plain language of the policy, Courts will simply declare what a policy says it is and not what is in the imagination of the policymaker,” the Court said. Kumar joined Army in 1996 As per the order, Kumar joined the Army in 1996. While posted at Kargil between 2003 and 2005 as part of ‘Operation Rakshak,’ he was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis. After his discharge in 2013, he received a Disability Pension. He later approached the Armed Forces Tribunal, seeking War Injury Pension instead of the disability pension. Kumar cited a policy letter of the Ministry of Defence from 2001, which covers disability arising from “operations specially notified by the Government.” The Tribunal allowed his claim in April 2024, finding that the ailment originated at Kargil where Kumar was posted. The High Court upheld this in August 2025. The Union government, however, moved the Supreme Court challenging the orders and arguing that the 2001 policy letter covered only “specifically notified operations such as Operation Sindoor or Operation Snow Leopard,” and not ongoing operations like ‘Rakshak” in Jammu and Kashmir or “Rhino” in Assam. The government also argued that Kumar's reading of the policy letter would make other clauses redundant and entitle “every soldier posted in J&K to the benefit.” The Court, however, refused to accept such submission. The bench said the government must go by what its policy actually says and not what it intended it to mean.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Union government to grant a ‘war injury pension’ to an Indian Army veteran who had developed “rheumatoid arthritis” during his posting at Kargil, ruling that the government cannot interpret its own policy in a way that “contradicts its plain wording” or leads to “arbitrary, irrational or discriminatory outcomes.”

A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed an appeal filed by the Union government challenging previous orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and the High Court that had directed it to pay the veteran, Narendra Kumar, a war injury pension instead of disability pension.
“While interpreting the plain language of the policy, Courts will simply declare what a policy says it is and not what is in the imagination of the policymaker,” the Court said.

As per the order, Kumar joined the Army in 1996. While posted at Kargil between 2003 and 2005 as part of ‘Operation Rakshak,’ he was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis. After his discharge in 2013, he received a Disability Pension. He later approached the Armed Forces Tribunal, seeking War Injury Pension instead of the disability pension.
Kumar cited a policy letter of the Ministry of Defence from 2001, which covers disability arising from “operations specially notified by the Government.”
The Tribunal allowed his claim in April 2024, finding that the ailment originated at Kargil where Kumar was posted. The High Court upheld this in August 2025.

news.headline: United Kingdom Plans 2029 Mission Utilizing Robotic Claws to Remove Orbital Space Junk
news.story_lead: The United Kingdom has announced plans for a groundbreaking space remediation mission in 2029 that will deploy giant robotic claws to capture two defunct satellites. The mission aims to drag the dead satellites into Earth's atmosphere, where friction will safely incinerate them upon re-entry. Public participation is also being invited to help select an official name for this first-of-its-kind cleanup project.
news.full_article_text:
### UK Space Clean-Up Mission Overview

In a landmark initiative to address the growing risks of orbital space junk, the United Kingdom is preparing a pioneering space clean-up mission scheduled to launch in 2029. The mission will deploy specialized spacecraft fitted with giant robotic claws designed to physically lock onto dead satellites operating in Earth's orbit.

### Operational Mechanism and Objectives

- **Targeting Defunct Satellites:** The robotic vehicle will approach and capture two non-functional satellites currently drifting in orbit.
- **Controlled Re-entry:** After securing the targets, the spacecraft will drag the satellites down towards the Earth's upper atmosphere.
- **Atmospheric Destruction:** Frictional heating created during atmospheric re-entry will cause the inactive satellites to burn up and disintegrate completely, removing them from orbit safely.
- **Public Naming Campaign:** As part of the rollout, UK officials have launched a public engagement campaign allowing members of the public to suggest and vote on the official name for the mission.

Giant robotic claws will be deployed to physically capture two dead satellites.
Captured satellites will be dragged into Earth's upper atmosphere to burn up safely.

The UK government has invited the public to participate in naming the mission.

### यूके अंतरिक्ष सफाई मिशन का विवरण

अंतरिक्ष मलबे से पैदा होने वाले खतरों से निपटने के लिए ब्रिटेन वर्ष 2029 में अपनी तरह का पहला अंतरिक्ष सफाई मिशन शुरू करने की तैयारी कर रहा है। इस मिशन के तहत विशेष अंतरिक्ष यान भेजे जाएंगे, जो विशाल रोबोटिक पंजों से लैस होंगे और कक्षा में मौजूद मृत उपग्रहों को पकड़ेंगे।

### कार्यप्रणाली और उद्देश्य

- **उपग्रहों को पकड़ना:** अंतरिक्ष यान रोबोटिक पंजों की मदद से दो निष्क्रिय उपग्रहों को मजबूती से ग्रिप करेगा।
- **वायुमंडलीय पुनः प्रवेश:** उपग्रहों को पकड़ने के बाद, यह मिशन यान उन्हें कक्षा से खींचकर पृथ्वी के ऊपरी वायुमंडल में लाएगा।
- **जलाकर नष्ट करना:** वायुमंडल में प्रवेश के दौरान घर्षण से पैदा होने वाली अत्यधिक गर्मी के कारण ये उपग्रह सुरक्षित रूप से जलकर नष्ट हो जाएंगे।
- **सार्वजनिक भागीदारी:** यूके ने जनता को इस मिशन के लिए आधिकारिक नाम का सुझाव देने और चुनने में मदद करने के लिए आमंत्रित किया है।
